text.en: Cancer is from the Latin word for crab, because tumours spread like claws. AIDS appeared in the 1980s; Dr Suniti Solomon in Chennai documented India's first case in 1985.

Cancer is abnormal, uncontrolled cell division that forms a tumour or neoplasm; spread of cancer cells to distant parts is metastasis.
Oncology is the study of cancer; benign tumours remain confined and malignant tumours invade other tissues.
Types by tissue: carcinomas (epithelial, about 85 percent), sarcomas (connective and muscle) and leukaemia (blood cancer).
Carcinogens include tobacco smoke, chewing betel and tobacco, asbestos, X-rays, gamma rays, UV rays and oncogenic viruses.
Treatment: surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy and immunotherapy with interferons.
Prevention: avoid tobacco, avoid excess radiation and sunlight, protect against industrial pollutants and detect early.
AIDS is caused by HIV, which attacks lymphocytes and makes the immune system fail.
HIV spreads by sexual contact, contaminated needles, infected blood transfusion and from mother to child; it does not spread by touch or ordinary contact.
Symptoms: swollen lymph nodes, fever, weight loss, chronic diarrhoea and repeated infections; confirmed by ELISA or Western blot; anti-retroviral drugs prolong life.
Control: screen blood, use disposable needles, safe sex, awareness, and never isolate people living with HIV.

problem.en: A friend says AIDS spreads by shaking hands. Correct this.

text.en: HIV spreads only through body fluids like blood and sexual fluids.
Touch, shared food or hugging do not spread HIV.
So people with HIV should not be isolated.

prompt.en: Distinguish a benign tumour from a malignant tumour.

requiredIdeas.en: Benign tumour stays in its organ
Malignant tumour invades and shows metastasis

points.en: HIV spreads only by body fluids; no isolation.
